deep.reconstruction:
Section 2 sets up a simplicial formalism for 'global stratifications' without tubes, meaning without tubular neighbourhoods or link data. The page's aim, read with the previous page, is to express the homotopy type of a stratified space whose pieces are K(π,1)'s, such as Teichmüller/moduli spaces and their compactifications, through a combinatorial diagram attached to the strata. Grothendieck works on a topological space X for now, but warns that X will later be an arbitrary topos. Everything must eventually be 'sheafified' over X. That step will force extra connectedness and local connectedness hypotheses, and he postpones any local-triviality (normal triviality) assumptions on the embeddings.

The data are as follows.
- I is an ordered set and (X_i)_{i∈I} a family of subspaces of X.
- (a) The X_i are closed and the family is locally finite.
- (b) i ≤ j implies X_i ⊂ X_j.
In modern terms these are the closed 'downward' pieces X_{≤i} of a poset-indexed stratification. The strata are recovered as X_i minus the union of the X_j with j<i.

He then defines X_{Δ0} = ⊔_i X_i = {(x,i) ∈ X×I | x ∈ X_i} with its canonical map to X. The next page continues as follows.
- The map X_{Δ0} → X is separated and finite (proper with finite fibres), and is a local immersion.
- X_{Δ1} = ⊔_{i≤j} Γ_{ij} ⊂ X_{Δ0}×X_{Δ0}, where Γ_{ij} is the graph of the inclusion X_i ⊂ X_j.
- The source map a is a covering, trivial over each X_i with fibre I_i = {j ≥ i}; the target map b is a local immersion.

This is the beginning of an internal category (eventually a simplicial object X_{Δ•}) in spaces or in a topos. It is the poset I 'spread out' over X: X_{Δn} = ⊔_{i0≤…≤in} X_{i0}, the nerve of the diagram i ↦ X_i over I. This is the scaffolding on which the 'integration' of homotopy types from the fundamental groupoids of the pieces is to be carried out.
errors: No real error. Small remark on the next page: the proviso 'donc rev. fini si les I_i sont finis' is automatic for nonempty X_i. A point x ∈ X_i lies in every X_j with j ≥ i, so local finiteness of the family already forces I_i to be finite.

The data do not by themselves define a stratification in the usual frontier-condition sense. Nothing yet requires the strata X_i \ ∪_{j<i} X_j to be disjoint or to cover X, and no frontier condition is imposed. Grothendieck explicitly defers such conditions.
Transcription: the phrase 'relatifs :' should read 'relatives à une', i.e. the constructions relating to a 'global stratification'.

ideas.what: Stratification encoded as a poset-indexed, increasing, locally finite family of closed subspaces, intended to work over an arbitrary topos ('topos stratifié').
ideas.modern_name: P-stratified space / stratified topos (closed subsets X_{≤p})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lurie (Higher Algebra, Appendix A, ~2009-2017); Barwick–Glasman–Haine, Exodromy (2018)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5-6 (tame/stratified spaces, dévissage) in spirit; the topos version is not published as far as known

ideas.what: Simplicial object / internal category X_{Δ•} with X_{Δ0} = ⊔X_i and X_{Δ1} = ⊔_{i≤j} Γ_{ij}, with étale source map and locally-immersive target map.
ideas.modern_name: Nerve of the diagram I → Spaces, i ↦ X_i (Grothendieck-construction / homotopy-colimit simplicial space); close to a Čech nerve for a closed cover indexed by a poset

ideas.what: Programme to express the homotopy type of a stratified space with K(π,1) strata via a diagram of fundamental groupoids of the strata, first without tubes and later with tubes.
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacPherson (exit paths, 1990s), Treumann 2009, Lurie, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka, Haine
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), discussion of tame topology and stratified structures of moduli spaces

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a stratification relative to an arbitrary topos, with the stratifying poset internalized as an étale-source internal category. He states that sheafification over the topos will require connectedness and local connectedness hypotheses. This anticipates the 'stratified topos / exodromy' framework of Barwick–Glasman–Haine, where stratified étale homotopy types of schemes are built from poset-stratified topoi.
missed.quote: par la suite X deviendra un topos quelconque ... devront "faisceautiser" sur X
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an early unpublished trace of the stratified-topos viewpoint. It is of historical interest for crediting the exodromy and stratified-homotopy programme, though the construction on this page itself is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine setup: poset-indexed closed filtration plus its nerve. Its interest is mainly historical, as evidence that around 1981 Grothendieck was formalizing stratifications over arbitrary topoi simplicially, a prelude to exit-path/exodromy ideas. No nontrivial result appears here.

Last line: 'on a un simplicial [?] canonique' should read 'on a un morphisme canonique', continuing as (3) X_{Δ0} → X on the next page.
